LESSON: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: DESCRIPTIVE FICTIONAL OR NON-FICTIONAL TEXTS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you describe things?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the main idea in each paragraph
2. answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: DESCRIPTIVE FICTIONAL OR NON-FICTIONAL TEXTS
This lesson teaches Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts for Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify the main idea in each paragraph
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts above.
2. Explain Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you describe things?
2. How can you tell what will happen in a story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the main idea in each paragraph
2. answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
